title: Earth’s magnetic field, crustal geology, and artificial EM
summary: Three different “magnetism” ideas kept separate on purpose: planetary main field models, crustal/volcanic place context, and human infrastructure—plus how to read them in Place.

sections.heading: Main field (what Place may show as µT / dip)
sections.body: The World Magnetic Model (WMM) and related services estimate Earth’s core-dominated magnetic field at a latitude, longitude, and elevation. Typical surface total intensity is tens of microtesla; inclination (dip) increases toward the poles; declination offsets magnetic from true north. These quantities change slowly (secular variation). They are geophysical estimates—not a reading of your body or of Wi‑Fi.

sections.heading: Crustal anomalies vs smooth models
sections.body: Finer models and grids (e.g. Enhanced Magnetic Model / EMAG-type products) add shorter-wavelength crustal magnetic anomalies from rock magnetization. Resolution is still regional (tens of kilometers class), not house-by-house. That is solid-Earth science used in geology and navigation error budgets—not a health meter for your bedroom.

sections.heading: Geology score in this app (volcano / magma proximity)
sections.body: Separately, the app scores “geological vitality” as distance to Holocene volcanic and magma-system anchors (Smithsonian GVP–derived catalogs and USGS lists). Influence uses inverse-square falloff (1/r²): full boost within ~100 km of an anchor, tapering to zero past ~750 km—so a volcano a continent away does not inflate your score. That is a transparent lifestyle proxy for living crustal systems—not the same number as total field F from WMM, and not a volcanic hazard product.

sections.heading: Artificial EM infrastructure
sections.body: Cell sites, masts, power plants, and dense urban electronics create non-native electromagnetic environments. They do not appear in WMM. This app’s artificial EM load score is an open-map proxy (e.g. OpenCelliD when available, OpenStreetMap masts and plants) plus a soft population/device-density bump from mapped building counts—useful for “how built-up is the RF/power landscape,” not a personal V/m measurement at your pillow.

sections.heading: Where Dr. Jack Kruse’s teaching is specific
sections.body: Kruse’s public work often binds latitude, geomagnetic environment, geology, and non-native EMF into one mitochondrial place story, including space-weather narratives in popular teaching. Those integrated lifestyle conclusions are his. The app deliberately separates layers—main field model, magma proximity, infrastructure proxy, daily habits—so you can see data sources without treating them as one medical score.

sections.heading: What is solid, what is framework
sections.body: Solid ground: WMM-style main field and crustal anomaly science; volcano catalogs; cell/mast maps as rough built-environment proxies. Framework: merging those layers into a personal disease risk number, or treating Place scores as body magnetometry. Daily levers remain habits: grounding, nature time, nnEMF blocks, Sleep Space.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Set your ZIP on Today → Place and read main field, geology, and artificial EM as separate rows. Log Grounding, Nature immersion, Low artificial field hour, and nnEMF reduction blocks when you practice them. Pair with the magnetosphere/SAA and North American inclination-drop lessons for regional context. Educational only—not relocation or medical advice.
